finding: Production database URL can disable or weaken TLS after validation
evidence: Verified offline against pinned pg parser: duplicate sslmode, nested connectionString, weak libpq modes, encoded keys with raw spaces or malformed escapes. Conditional on configuration; no deployed unsafe URL established.
acceptance: Reject ambiguous controls and canonicalize accepted production TLS URLs; both application and migration URLs must retain certificate and hostname verification.

finding: Forbidden email and viewer-grant ownership branch remains executable
evidence: Verified with pure claim and real completion wiring: OWNER_SELF_SERVICE_CLAIM=true lets a report recipient supply their own lead email and grant and permanently attach the scan. Default off mitigates exposure.
acceptance: Remove the mutation branch and runtime switch; existing verified owner resumes, Google/staff assignment remain; legacy flag=true cannot create or attach.

finding: Application website checks can fetch private services and unbounded bodies
evidence: Verified injected-transport regression: raw fetch follows redirects to private destinations and reads the entire body before slicing. Workspace snapshot and scheduled verifier use this path; the separately hardened scan-engine fetch does not protect it. No internal live target contacted.
acceptance: Resolve only public addresses and pin sockets; revalidate every redirect; cap streamed bytes at 512KiB; bound time and cancellation; reject non-HTML/unsupported encoding as unavailable; preserve public HTTP and final URL.

finding: Pinned dependencies have security advisories requiring release review
evidence: Registry audit completed: 45 reported vulnerability instances, 42 advisory records including five critical Next records. Server Action DoS preconditions exist; optimizer RCE is conditional on attacker-controlled allowed image bytes. Other critical prerequisites not found. See dependency-advisory-triage.csv.
acceptance: Select reviewed Next >=16.4.1 and coherent sharp >=0.35.5 or later fixes for this snapshot; verify framework/auth/renderer gates. Preserve Neon SDK pin unless its change is separately approved. Never equate advisory count with proved exploits.

finding: Raw Stripe and provider errors can expose payloads in logs
evidence: Code and installed SDK confirm signature error stores enumerable payload and signature header. Expired valid events carry billing/customer data; invalid events allow log injection when webhook secret configured. Other billing/OAuth catches also log raw errors.
acceptance: Replace raw objects/messages with fixed category and generated correlation ID; sentinel request, signature, token and SQL details must never appear in logs.

finding: Google claim failure can strand permanently attached ownership
evidence: Code-only: create workspace and write-once attach happen before encryption and connection storage. Failure leaves attachment; retry returns already_claimed. OAuth flag ships off; hosted configuration not inspected.
acceptance: Encrypt before mutation, then atomically create/reuse workspace, attach job and install encrypted connection with retry semantics. Inject failure at each stage against owned SQL fixtures.

finding: Workflow evaluator can report failed generation as passing
evidence: Verified offline: locale-market-zh-tw-on-hk with null model returns pass:true, notes:[run_failed], cost0 despite corpus expecting a generated version. Pass only checks excluded warnings; many expected assertions are ignored.
acceptance: Evaluate required corpus states/version/facts/prompt assertions and fail unexpected model failures; distinguish explicitly expected failures. No live paid model required to repair evaluator.
test: Null, throwing, malformed and valid injected-model evaluation tests

finding: Two checkout sessions can create duplicate subscriptions and conflicting tiers
evidence: Code-only: 30-second idempotency buckets allow a lite owner two outstanding sessions across buckets; both can complete. Each subscription independently controls one tier, so cancelling either can downgrade the workspace. Commercial gate is closed by default; no Stripe calls made.
acceptance: Choose one subscription per workspace and pending-session/reconciliation rules, then persist session/subscription identity under concurrency control. Repeated checkout and cancellation tests must preserve the chosen entitlement.
test: Mocked Stripe / owned SQL duplicate session and subscription lifecycle tests

finding: Secret boundary gate misses real server secret names
evidence: Code-only gap, not a current leak: scanner sets OPENROUTER_API_KEY but runtime reads OPENROUTER_KEY, OPENCODE_API_KEY, LLM_API_KEY. Also omits report-access, mail-unsubscribe, cron, Google Places and fallback provider keys.
acceptance: Expand valid sentinel inventory to actual server secret names; verify a deliberately exposed sentinel is detected and clean build stays clean.
test: Built-artifact sentinel gate and name-parity checks

finding: Eight runtime-orphan application helpers remain maintained and tested
paths: lib/llm-translate.ts:1; lib/analytics/events.ts:1; lib/scanner/draft.ts:1; lib/report/competitor-gap.ts:1; lib/evidence/inline-print-media.ts:1; lib/localized-field.ts:1; lib/scan-modes.ts:1; components/visual/page-transition.tsx:1
evidence: AST reachability plus symbol searches: eight files, 665 lines, with no runtime callers or only tests. No unused direct runtime dependency established. Alias modules, generated types, demo data, contracts and vendored code deliberately excluded.
acceptance: Remove confirmed obsolete helpers and their isolated tests in a separate cleanup, or document retention purpose. Do not mount them into product.
test: Typecheck, root tests and build after removal

finding: JSON null bodies cause unhandled exceptions in older routes
evidence: Code-only: req.json succeeds with null, TypeScript cast does not validate it, then field dereference throws outside parse catch. No authorization bypass established.
acceptance: Parse a bounded non-array object before dereference; malformed requests return 400 and known dependency failures return controlled unavailable responses.
test: null, arrays, oversized and malformed JSON route tests

finding: Successful mutations can permanently lose accountability events
evidence: Code-only: business writes commit before best-effort audit insert; insertion failures are swallowed without durable retry. Version/export transaction paths already audit atomically.
acceptance: Make the required accountability durable with an atomic event write or transactional outbox. Test both mutation failure and retry so successful work cannot permanently lose its event; best-effort loss does not satisfy the existing guardrail.
test: Injected audit-write failure and transaction/outbox recovery tests

finding: Failed Blob compensation leaves untracked private objects
evidence: Code-only: failed asset row insertion triggers best-effort object delete whose failure is swallowed. Database-only lifecycle operations do not constitute complete Blob/identity erasure.
acceptance: Choose retention periods and erasure responsibilities; persist deletion retries or implement bounded namespace orphan sweep with receipts.
test: Upload success + SQL failure + delete failure / erasure reconciliation tests

finding: Operator audit identity may select another user sharing the email
evidence: Code-only: verified app user ID is available but operator lookup uses lower(email) LIMIT1. app_users permits multiple provider subjects per email. Email allowlist still enforces operator authorization; attribution can be wrong.
acceptance: Use the verified mapped user ID for operator attribution; test two app identities with the same verified email.

finding: Asset list and preview renewal apply different location read rules
evidence: Code-only: list signs all workspace assets; renewal restricts scoped managers by stored location. Current CLAUDE broad-read contract allows reading workspace evidence, so this is inconsistent renewal/policy, not a proved cross-tenant leak.
acceptance: Align preview renewal with the established broad workspace evidence read contract. A future change to location-restricted reads requires a separate product decision and must change listing and renewal together.
test: Scoped manager list, expired URL and renewal tests

finding: Claim resume recognizes only the earliest owned workspace
evidence: Code-only: ownedWorkspace selects accepted owner rows ORDER BY created_at,id LIMIT1. A report already attached to a second workspace owned by the same user falls through to requires_verification. Existing behavior; normal workspace membership reads remain available.
acceptance: For a report carrying workspace_id, check accepted ownership for that exact workspace instead of comparing against the earliest owned workspace; preserve fail-closed behavior for other owners.
test: Two owned workspaces, second report resume, revoked ownership regression
